sub_criteria.name: agentic system design
sub_criteria.text: Describes or evaluates an LLM agent that searches literature iteratively: query reformulation, multi-round search, citation-graph traversal, or crawling, rather than a single retrieval call.

sub_criteria.name: baseline search recall
sub_criteria.text: Reports how much of a target set a single-query or Boolean database search actually retrieves, giving a recall or coverage number the agentic systems can be measured against.

sub_criteria.name: benchmark construction
sub_criteria.text: Says how an evaluation set for literature search or deep research was built - where the gold papers came from, how queries were sampled, what the annotation protocol was.

sub_criteria.name: retrieval and reranking
sub_criteria.text: Contributes the retrieval or reranking method underneath: dense or hybrid retrieval, LLM rerankers, citation-aware ranking, or evidence on which component carries the gain.

sub_criteria.name: gains that fail
sub_criteria.text: Reports a replication failure, a weak or unbeaten baseline, benchmark leakage or construction that inflates scores, or a gain that vanishes under a different set or metric.

items.abstract_600: Query Reformulation (QR) is a set of techniques used to transform a user's original search query to a text that better aligns with the user's intent and improves their search experience. Recently, zero-shot QR has been a promising approach due to its ability to exploit knowledge inherent in large language models. items.abstract_600: This paper presents a domain-specific implementation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) tailored to the Fair Use Doctrine in U.S. copyright law. Motivated by the increasing prevalence of DMCA takedowns and the lack of accessible legal support for content creators, we propose a structured approach that combines semantic search with legal knowledge graphs and court citation networks to improve retrieval quality and reasoning reliability. items.abstract_600: Anemia during pregnancy affects more than one-third of women globally, with the heaviest burden in low- and middle-income countries. items.abstract_600: Academic paper search is an essential task for efficient literature discovery and scientific advancement. While dense retrieval has advanced various ad-hoc searches, it often struggles to match the underlying academic concepts between queries and documents, which is critical for paper search. items.abstract_600: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in various reasoning and generation tasks. items.abstract_600: As cosmological simulations and their associated software become increasingly complex, physicists face the challenge of searching through vast amounts of literature and user manuals to extract simulation parameters from dense academic papers, each using different models and formats. items.abstract_600: Diagnosing failure patterns in Deep Research Agents (DRAs) remains a critical challenge. items.abstract_600: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) enhances large language models (LLMs) by integrating external knowledge retrieval to improve factual consistency and reduce hallucinations.
